# Marginalia

The first correction appeared in October, in a copy of *Wuthering Heights* that had been checked out forty-one times. Marisol found it while flipping through the returned stack on Tuesday morning: a faint pencil mark beside the sentence about Heathcliff being "a dark-skinned gypsy." The word *skinned* had been underlined, and in the margin, in small, precise handwriting: *Brontë wrote "a gipsy" in the 1847 edition. Later editions altered it. Worth knowing.*

Marisol frowned. She was the head librarian of the Port Alden Public Library, a squat brick building two blocks from the harbor where the fishing boats came in, and she took defacement of books personally. But this wasn't defacement, exactly. It was pencil, not pen. Light enough to erase. And it was, she confirmed after some digging that evening, correct.

The second note came three weeks later, in a biography of Magellan. *He didn't die at Mactan thinking he'd circumnavigated the globe,* the margin said. *He knew the Spice Islands lay west of the antimeridian. Give him credit for the math, at least.*

By December, Mar
